presentation.label: RAVE STAB
presentation.summary: SY RAVE: a six-voice digital chord stab, thirteen chords and nine voicings a step can lock, detune, saw to pulse, a strum and a pitch drop, through the Rytm's own analog filter and AMP.
presentation.overview: An original chord voice computed on the Rytm's ColdFire at 48 kHz. Six band-limited oscillators play a chord in a voicing, both taken at each hit so a pattern can lock a progression step by step. DET spreads them against each other, WAV runs from saw through square to a narrow pulse and PCH drops or scoops the chord into its pitch at the hit, the zap of a rave stab. The track's own analog filter, AMP and OVR shape it: the filter's envelope makes the stab's sweep. EURK keeps the chord a musician found by accident in HH Alloy's metal oscillators.
highlights: Thirteen chords on CHD, nine voicings on VOI, each lockable per step.
Played chromatically: the note transposes the whole chord.
DET from exact to 30 cents of spread, WAV from saw to a 12 % pulse.
Tap the TUN encoder for the register: an octave down, two, at the note or up.
usage: Select the BD track, press FUNC + SRC, choose SY RAVE and press YES.
Close the filter and give it a short filter envelope for the classic stab.
Lock CHD and VOI on steps for a chord progression on one track.

access.location: The machine list of the BD, SD or BT track: SY RAVE, in the SY section. Its SYNTH page.
steps: Select a track and press FUNC + SRC.
Choose SY RAVE and press YES.
On the SYNTH page, tap the TUN encoder to step the register.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, on the Modwerk base's digital voices.
Offered on the BD, SD and BT tracks only until its cost is measured on a unit.
Not yet heard on a unit.

tests.summary: Host: 31 checks of pitch, the thirteen chords, voicings, the hit's latch, waves, band-limiting, the strum, the held level, the pitch drop, levels, velocity and smoothing (tools/host_test.c). On a MKII (RH01-RH03): the page, the CPU (6.76 % of a block a voice) and the developer's listening.
